note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Omagh rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. For the first time in 25 years four divisions were contested (Bencran, Gortin, Maine, Moyle), three by Anti-Partitionists and one by an Independent, all against Unionists. 'Seventeen Unionists and seventeen Anti-Partitionists were returned unopposed, but in one Nationalist division no nomination was received and the retiring member will be deemed re-elected'; four new members came in unopposed (Ulster Herald, 21 May 1949, p. 5). The unopposed members are recorded from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 11 June 1949, p. 2), read from the page OCR. Tattymoyle has no candidate in the notice's name columns; its column 6 names the retiring councillor, Peter Connolly, as re-elected (read on the block image, 7 Nov 2026).
